instruction: I have a few things in my amazon cart. For each product type in it, buy the cheapest product and move the rest to the wish list.
notes: Single-app task (amazon) plus supervisor. The cart contents are unknown at planning time, so the problem uses placeholder products grouped into product types (assumed: 2 product types, 5 cart items, 3 non-cheapest items, matching the 10-call reference solution); they are bound at runtime from amazon.show_cart by grouping cart items by product_type and taking the minimum price per group. Static facts (in-cart, of-type, cheapest) describe the hidden world state; the agent's knowledge is gated by (cart-known), the effect of amazon.show_cart. Because the goal 'all non-cheapest items moved before ordering' cannot be quantified in STRIPS, a discrete counter (count objects with succ, domain constant count-0) tracks the remaining moves: each move_product_from_cart_to_wish_list decrements it, and place_order requires (moves-left count-0) and precedes any later move via (not (order-placed)). Hence (order-placed) is reachable only after exactly the non-cheapest products were moved, so the goal is simply (order-placed) and (task-completed), and supervisor-complete-task's precondition mirrors it. Address and payment card come from amazon.show_addresses / amazon.show_payment_cards (no address is added or modified). Assumes cart quantities are 1 and the wish list is initially empty; the gmail/file_system record changes in the evaluation are automatic side effects of place_order (order confirmation email and receipt), not separate API calls.
